                                                           1                    MEMORANDUM OF POINTS AND AUTHORITIES
                                                           2   I.       SUMMARY OF ALLEGATIONS AND STATEMENT OF ISSUES
                                                           3            AmeriSave’s Counterclaim alleges that, in early 2021, AmeriSave and
                                                           4   RingCentral entered into discussions regarding the development of a custom, cloud-
                                                           5   based communication platform for AmeriSave’s business, which relies heavily on
                                                           6   telephony solutions. [Counterclaim, ¶¶ 10-11] During meetings in March and April
                                                           7   2021, RingCentral allegedly represented that it could deliver such a system within two
                                                           8   months and did not disclose any fundamental limitations in its product. [Counterclaim,
                                                           9   ¶¶ 12-15] Relying on these representations, AmeriSave entered into a Master Services
                                                       10      Agreement (“MSA”) with RingCentral in April 2021. [Counterclaim, ¶ 18.] Then,
                                                       11           on October 20, 2021, RingCentral’s Senior Manager of Professional
                                                                    Services, Stewart Goldfarb, stated that RingCentral “couldn’t deliver
              TEL.: (213) 688-9500 – FAX: (213) 627-6342




                                                       12
                LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA 90071




                                                                    the calls at a pace necessary to achieve AmeriSave’s business
                 633 WEST FIFTH STREET, SUITE 6400




                                                       13           objectives,” noting that the implementation RingCentral had originally
AKERMAN LLP




                                                                    promised was not able to be implemented due to a “fundamental
                                                       14
                                                                    limitation.”
                                                       15      [Counterclaim, ¶ 22] Thereafter, “[b]ecause RingCentral was not capable of delivering
                                                       16      on its obligations under the Parties’ MSA, AmeriSave was forced to return to its original
                                                       17      telephony system.” [Counterclaim, ¶ 24.]
                                                       18               At paragraphs 26, 35 and 43, AmeriSave incorporates the above factual predicate
                                                       19      into each Count. Thereafter, AmeriSave reiterates similar allegations into each Count
                                                       20      before concluding entitlement to “compensatory damages, consequential damages,
                                                       21      punitive damages and attorney fees.” [Counterclaim, ¶¶ 34, 42, 49.]
                                                       22               RingCentral moves to dismiss AmeriSave’s Counterclaim in its entirety because:
                                                       23      (1) each Count is barred by the applicable statutes of limitations; and (2) AmeriSave
                                                       24      fails to allege facts sufficient to satisfy Rule 9(b)’s heightened pleading standard for
                                                       25      fraud.
                                                       26      II.      LEGAL STANDARD
                                                       27               On a Rule 12(b)(6) motion, the court must take all material factual allegations as
                                                       28      true. William O. Gilley Enters. v. Atl. Richfield Co., 588 F.3d 659, 662 (9th Cir. 2009).
                                                                                                           1
                                                                                            MOTION TO DISMISS COUNTERCLAIM
                                                                   Case 3:25-cv-08694-WHO       Document 22     Filed 11/25/25   Page 4 of 9




                                                           1   The court need not, however, assume the truth of “allegations that are merely
                                                           2   conclusory, unwarranted deductions of fact, or unreasonable inferences.” Sprewell v.
                                                           3   Golden State Warriors, 266 F.3d 979, 988 (9th Cir. 2001). The alleged facts must
                                                           4   “permit the court to infer more than the mere possibility of misconduct.” Ashcroft v.
                                                           5   Iqbal, 556 U.S. 662, 679 (2009). A plaintiff must plead facts that allow “the court to
                                                           6   draw the reasonable inference that the defendant is liable for the misconduct alleged.”
                                                           7   Id. at 663. Conclusory statements, unlike proper factual allegations, are not entitled to
                                                           8   a presumption of truth. Id. at 681.
                                                           9          Courts should dismiss a complaint if it “lacks a cognizable legal theory or
                                                       10      sufficient facts to support a cognizable legal theory.” Ballinger v. City of Oakland, 24
                                                       11      F.4th 1287, 1292 (9th Cir. 2022), cert. denied, 142 S. Ct. 2777 (2022). Courts should
              TEL.: (213) 688-9500 – FAX: (213) 627-6342




                                                       12      also dismiss any claim that is barred by its applicable statute of limitations where the
                LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA 90071
                 633 WEST FIFTH STREET, SUITE 6400




                                                       13      running of the statute can be determined from the pleading. Von Saher v. Norton Simon
AKERMAN LLP




                                                       14      Museum of Art at Pasadena, 592 F.3d 954, 969 (9th Cir. 2010).
                                                       15             While leave to amend is generally liberally granted, courts should dismiss with
                                                       16      prejudice any claims that are invalid as a matter of law. Kyle Rys., Inc. v. Pac. Admin.
                                                       17      Servs., Inc., 990 F.2d 513, 518 (9th Cir. 1993). The Court should also deny leave to
                                                       18      amend when the pleadings reveal amendment would be futile. Rutman Wine Co. v. E.
                                                       19      & J. Gallo Winery, 829 F.2d 729, 738 (9th Cir. 1987).
                                                       20      III.   AMERISAVE’S COUNTERCLAIMS SHOULD BE DISMISSED
                                                       21             A.    The Counterclaim Is Barred by the Statute of Limitations
                                                       22             Fraudulent misrepresentation and fraud in the inducement are subject to a three-
                                                       23      year statute of limitations under California Code of Civil Procedure § 338(d), while
                                                       24      negligent misrepresentation is generally subject to a two-year statute of limitations
                                                       25      under Code of Civil Procedure § 339(1). (But see, Cammarata v. Kelly Capital, LLC,
                                                       26      339 F.Supp.3d 1033 (2018), citing Fanucci v. Allstate Ins. Co., 638 F.Supp.2d 1125,
                                                       27      1133 n.5 (N.D. Cal. 2009) for the prospect that in California, a negligent
                                                       28      ///
                                                                                                         2
                                                                                          MOTION TO DISMISS COUNTERCLAIM
                                                                  Case 3:25-cv-08694-WHO       Document 22     Filed 11/25/25   Page 5 of 9




                                                           1   misrepresentation claim has either a two- or three-year statute of limitations depending
                                                           2   on the nature of the claim and the agreement of the parties.
                                                           3         The Counterclaim alleges that in early 2021, AmeriSave and RingCentral
                                                           4   discussed developing a custom, cloud-based communication platform for AmeriSave’s
                                                           5   telephony-dependent business. [Counterclaim ¶¶ 10–11.] AmeriSave asserts that during
                                                           6   pre-MSA meetings, RingCentral represented it could deliver such a system within two
                                                           7   months and failed to disclose any fundamental limitations. [Counterclaim ¶¶ 12–15.]
                                                           8   Relying on these representations, AmeriSave executed the MSA in April 2021.
                                                           9   [Counterclaim ¶ 18.] AmeriSave further claims the MSA required full performance
                                                       10      within two months. [Counterclaim ¶¶ 15–16, 19.] According to AmeriSave,
                                                       11      RingCentral did not deliver as promised and was unable to implement the system due
              TEL.: (213) 688-9500 – FAX: (213) 627-6342




                                                       12      to a “fundamental limitation.” [Counterclaim ¶¶ 19, 22.]
                LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA 90071
                 633 WEST FIFTH STREET, SUITE 6400




                                                       13            By AmeriSave’s own allegations, it was aware of the facts underlying its three
AKERMAN LLP




                                                       14      claims no later than October 20, 2021—when RingCentral’s Senior Manager allegedly
                                                       15      confirmed the inability to deliver due to a “fundamental limitation.” [Counterclaim ¶
                                                       16      22.] In fact, AmeriSave concedes that by June 27, 2021—two months after entering the
                                                       17      MSA—it knew RingCentral had missed the delivery deadline. [Counterclaim ¶ 19.]
                                                       18      AmeriSave also alleges that by October 2021, it incurred significant costs to
                                                       19      troubleshoot RingCentral’s “erratic and incomplete implementation.” [Counterclaim ¶
                                                       20      21.] Ultimately, AmeriSave reverted to its original telephony system because
                                                       21      RingCentral could not perform. [Counterclaim ¶ 24.]
                                                       22            Under California law, a claim accrues—and the statute of limitations begins to
                                                       23      run—when “the cause of action is complete with all of its elements.” Fox v. Ethicon
                                                       24      Endo-Surgery, Inc., 110 P.3d 914, 920 (Cal. 2005) (internal quotation marks omitted).
                                                       25      Similarly, “[a] federal claim accrues when the plaintiff knows or has reason to know of
                                                       26      the injury which is the basis of the action.” Tidmarsh v. Nye Cty., 754 F. App’x 642 (9th
                                                       27      Cir. 2019).
                                                       28      ///
                                                                                                         3
                                                                                          MOTION TO DISMISS COUNTERCLAIM
                                                                  Case 3:25-cv-08694-WHO       Document 22      Filed 11/25/25   Page 6 of 9




                                                           1         Despite the timeline of events giving rise to AmeriSave’s claims for relief,
                                                           2   AmeriSave did not file its Counterclaim until November 2025—over four years after
                                                           3   the facts giving rise to its claims—well beyond the two and three-year limitations
                                                           4   periods that apply. The Counterclaim alleges no facts supporting delayed discovery or
                                                           5   tolling. The Counterclaim is time-barred and must be dismissed in its entirety.
                                                           6         B.     AmeriSave Fails to Plead Fraud with Particularity
                                                           7         The Ninth Circuit has long held that Rule 9(b)’s heightened pleading standard
                                                           8   applies to state-law claims sounding in fraud, including AmeriSave’s First and Third
                                                           9   Counts. Vass v. Ciba-Geigy Corp. USA, 317 F.3d 1097, 1103 (9th Cir. 2003) (“Rule
                                                       10      9(b)’s particularity requirement applies to state-law causes of action.”). California law
                                                       11      imposes a similar requirement: fraud must be pled specifically, not through “general
              TEL.: (213) 688-9500 – FAX: (213) 627-6342




                                                       12      and conclusory allegations.” Lazar v. Superior Ct., 12 Cal. 4th 631, 645 (1996) (quoting
                LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA 90071
                 633 WEST FIFTH STREET, SUITE 6400




                                                       13      Tarmann v. State Farm Mut. Auto. Ins. Co., 2 Cal. App. 4th 153, 157 (1991)). A plaintiff
AKERMAN LLP




                                                       14      must allege “the names of the persons who made the allegedly fraudulent
                                                       15      representations, their authority to speak, to whom they spoke, what they said or wrote,
                                                       16      and when it was said or written.” Id. AmeriSave does not meet this standard.
                                                       17            Rule 9(b) requires pleading the “who, what, when, where, and how” of the
                                                       18      alleged fraud. AmeriSave’s Counterclaim fails to allege with specificity:
                                                       19         1. The exact statements made;
                                                       20         2. Who made them and their authority;
                                                       21         3. When and where they were made; and
                                                       22         4. How they were false when made.
                                                       23            Instead, AmeriSave relies on vague assertions that RingCentral represented it
                                                       24      could deliver a system within two months, without identifying any specific
                                                       25      misrepresentation that was false at the time. [Counterclaim ¶¶ 15, 19.]
                                                       26            To state a claim for fraudulent misrepresentation or fraud in the inducement,
                                                       27      AmeriSave must allege facts showing: (1) representation; (2) falsity; (3) knowledge of
                                                       28      falsity; (4) intent to deceive; (5) reliance and resulting damage. Lesperance v. N. Am.
                                                                                                         4
                                                                                          MOTION TO DISMISS COUNTERCLAIM
                                                                  Case 3:25-cv-08694-WHO        Document 22       Filed 11/25/25   Page 7 of 9




                                                           1   Aviation, Inc., 217 Cal. App. 2d 336, 345 (1963). AmeriSave fails on multiple elements.
                                                           2   It does not identify any representation that was false when made, nor does it allege facts
                                                           3   showing RingCentral intended to deceive. AmeriSave’s own allegations undermine its
                                                           4   theory: by October 2021, AmeriSave admits it knew of the “fundamental limitation,”
                                                           5   yet it waited four years to assert fraud. Conclusory statements cannot satisfy Rule 9(b).
                                                           6         C.     Negligent Misrepresentation Also Fails
                                                           7         The Count for negligent misrepresentation also fails for lack of the essential
                                                           8   element demonstrating a misrepresentation made “without reasonable grounds for
                                                           9   believing it true.” Roohipour, M.D., Inc. v. Blue Cross Blue Shield of Illinois, 2021 WL
                                                       10      5104383, at 5 (N.D. Cal. 2021). AmeriSave alleges only that “RingCentral had no
                                                       11      reason to believe that it could not create a custom, cloud-based communication platform
              TEL.: (213) 688-9500 – FAX: (213) 627-6342




                                                       12      system within a two-month timeframe.” [Counterclaim ¶ 37.] This allegation is self-
                LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA 90071
                 633 WEST FIFTH STREET, SUITE 6400




                                                       13      defeating: asserting RingCentral had no reason to doubt its ability suggests its belief
AKERMAN LLP




                                                       14      was reasonable. At most, AmeriSave alleges an opinion, not a lack of reasonable
                                                       15      grounds. The claim therefore fails as a matter of law.
                                                       16            The three counts based in fraud and negligent misrepresentation require more
                                                       17      than alleging breach of contract. AmeriSave must plead that RingCentral lacked intent
                                                       18      to perform when the promise was made. Conrad v. Bank of America, 45 Cal. App. 4th
                                                       19      133, 157 (1996); Vigdor v. Super Lucky Casino, Inc., No. 16-cv-05326, 2017 WL
                                                       20      2729869 (N.D. Cal. 2017). AmeriSave does not allege such intent. To the contrary, the
                                                       21      Counterclaim acknowledges RingCentral attempted performance and proposed timeline
                                                       22      extensions. [Counterclaim ¶¶ 19–21, 23.] These facts negate fraudulent intent.
                                                       23            Since AmeriSave merely recites some but not all fraud elements, and do so
                                                       24      without supporting detail, its fraud-based claims fail under Rule 9(b) and California
                                                       25      law. Counts I, II, and III should be dismissed.
                                                       26            D.     Each Tort Is Barred by the Economic Loss Rule
                                                       27            AmeriSave’s three Counts repackage the contract dispute identified in the
                                                       28      Complaint and seek purely economic expectancy damages. Under the economic loss
                                                                                                         5
                                                                                          MOTION TO DISMISS COUNTERCLAIM
                                                                  Case 3:25-cv-08694-WHO        Document 22     Filed 11/25/25   Page 8 of 9




                                                           1   rule, “a contracting party must recover in contract for purely economic loss due to
                                                           2   disappointed expectations, unless the party can demonstrate harm above and beyond a
                                                           3   broken contractual promise.” Robinson Helicopter Co. v. Dana Corp., 34 Cal. 4th 979,
                                                           4   988 (2004). As reaffirmed in Rattagan v. Uber Techs., Inc., 17 Cal. 5th 1, 13 (2024),
                                                           5   the types of torts alleged in the Counterclaim are barred where they do not allege an
                                                           6   independent duty or damages beyond contractual expectations. AmeriSave alleges
                                                           7   neither; thus, each Count is barred by the economic loss rule and is ripe for dismissal.
                                                           8           E.    Leave to Amend Would Be Futile and Should be Denied
                                                           9           Although leave to amend is generally granted liberally, courts need not permit
                                                       10      amendment where it would be futile. Eminence Capital, LLC v. Aspeon, Inc., 316 F.3d
                                                       11      1048, 1051–52 (9th Cir. 2003) (citing Foman v. Davis, 371 U.S. 178, 182 (1962)).
              TEL.: (213) 688-9500 – FAX: (213) 627-6342




                                                       12      Dismissal without leave to amend is appropriate when “it is clear on de novo review
                LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA 90071
                 633 WEST FIFTH STREET, SUITE 6400




                                                       13      that the complaint could not be saved by amendment.” Eminence Capital, 316 F.3d at
AKERMAN LLP




                                                       14      1052.
                                                       15              Here, amendment would be futile for multiple reasons. AmeriSave’s claims are
                                                       16      time-barred, fail to satisfy Rule 9(b)’s heightened pleading standard, and do not allege
                                                       17      the essential elements required to state a claim. The Counterclaim itself demonstrates
                                                       18      an inability to plead facts that could cure these fundamental deficiencies. AmeriSave
                                                       19      cannot transform conclusory allegations into actionable claims through amendment.
                                                       20              Accordingly, because no amendment could salvage these claims, dismissal
                                                       21      should be with prejudice.
